title: [finding] No reader anywhere answers a cross-repo Blocked-by: question — H14 can only decline, and 58 of 67 cross-repo cards carry no repo:* label to decline on
body:
Filed out of the review of PR #13990 (card #13975), by the `domain:devx` execution PM seat. #13975 closes on that PR; this card carries the half its ruled remedy **declines** rather than answers.

## What #13990 shipped, and what it deliberately did not

H14's strip direction now **declines** on a card carrying any `repo:*` label, instead of prescribing a strip it cannot justify. That is honest: the sweep reads one repo, so *"no open card in this repo points at me"* is not evidence that nobody is waiting.

⛔ **But declining is not answering.** Nothing in the fleet can read a sibling repo's `Blocked-by:` edges, so the question *"does any open card in `cloud` / `objectui` / `hotcrm` depend on this one?"* has **no reader anywhere**.

## ⭐ The measurement that makes this worth a card

The ruled predicate — *"carries any `repo:*` label"* — covers **2 of the 5** live strip rows, and **2 of the 4** cards #13975 itself said must not be stripped:

| card | `repo:*` label | H14-B today |
|--:|:--|:--|
| #12931 | `repo:cloud` | declines ✅ |
| #12580 | `repo:hotcrm` | declines ✅ |
| **#13439** | **none** | **still accused** ⚠️ |
| **#13568** | **none** | **still accused** ⚠️ |

⚠️ #13439 and #13568 are precisely the two whose off-repo waiters #13975's filing recorded on the record — cloud#1451 waiting on #13439's ruling, and #13568's own ruling commissioning an objectui card. **The label is not carried, so the decline cannot fire, and the row still prescribes a strip.**

Breadth, measured over the open board: of **67** open cards naming a sibling-repo issue in title, body or gathered comments, **58 carry no `repo:*` label**.

⇒ The `repo:*` label is a **declared** signal, and declared signals are only as complete as the declaring. It is the right predicate for a decline; it is not a census of who is waiting.

## The remedy — and the two that were already refused

**In scope: a cross-repo `Blocked-by:` reader.** Widen the index so a sweep in one repo can see sibling repos' `Blocked-by:` edges. Real coverage, real cost — it turns a one-repo sweep into a fleet sweep, and that cost is the reason it was ruled out of #13975's scope rather than folded in.

⛔ **Refused, with reasons on the record — do not re-propose either:**

1. **A textual proxy** (decline when the body or comments name a sibling-repo issue). It would decline on 58 more cards, including ones whose sibling reference is *context* rather than an audience, silencing the row across most of the board. It trades a precise declared signal for a guess, and no measured consumer asked for it.
2. **Backfilling `repo:*` onto the 58.** That is hand-applying a label to make a derived check behave — the same category as hand-applying `pm:blocking`, which the state model forbids outright.

## ⚠️ Read this before scoping it

`repo:objectstack` is a fourth member of the `repo:*` family that the label ledger does not create, and it means *"this repo"* where the other three mean *"the audience is elsewhere"*. **#13991** owns that question. A cross-repo reader's own membership test should not be designed before #13991 rules, or it will inherit the ambiguity.

## Re-check

```
node scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs | grep -E "H14 .*carried while no open"
```

Rows that still fire are the population this card would answer; rows marked `UNJUDGED` are the ones #13990 already declines.

Left unassigned and ungraded — the triage seat grades.
